name: Change of base and the log chain
formula: \log_a b = \frac{\log_c b}{\log_c a}, \qquad \log_a b \cdot \log_b c = \log_a c, \qquad \log_a b = \frac{1}{\log_b a} \quad (\text{bases positive and } \ne 1,\ \text{arguments positive})
whenToUse: Logs with different bases appear together, especially a product of logs where each base matches the previous argument.
pitfall: The new base goes in BOTH the top and the bottom, and the original base ends up on the bottom. Writing $\frac{\log_c a}{\log_c b}$ gives the reciprocal.
derivation: If $a^p = b$ then taking $\log_c$ of both sides gives $p \log_c a = \log_c b$, so $p = \frac{\log_c b}{\log_c a}$.
